claude_only.name: Which system is the authoritative issuer of this revision identifier, and is it the same system that holds the host entity's master record?
What identifier form is used for the revision, and is it opaque or does it encode meaning?
Is the revision identifier guaranteed never to be reused or re-pointed at different content, and what enforces that?
How does the revision identifier relate to the persistent identifier of the versioned entity itself?
Which validator may be derived from this revision for conditional access, and is it strong or weak?
Which version designation grammar does this entity declare, and where is that declaration published?
Does an increment in the designation carry a normative compatibility promise, or is the designation descriptive only?
Against which declared public surface is a breaking change judged?
How are pre-release, post-release, development, epoch and build or local qualifiers handled, and do they affect precedence?
Does a version-independent identifier exist for the entity series, and what does dereferencing it yield?
Which relations assert that this revision is a version of the series and which assert the series' current version?
How is 'latest' defined when concurrent branches or contexts each have a most recent revision?
May the series identifier be used as an evidentiary citation target, or must citations pin a revision?
Is the order over revisions total or partial, and what produces partiality?
Which fields participate in precedence comparison and which are explicitly ignored?
Can ordering be derived from the identifier or label alone, or must the predecessor graph be traversed?
Which revision is currently in force for each branch, and who may move that pointer?
May the head move backwards to an earlier revision, and how is that recorded?
Which revisions does this revision directly succeed, and is the predecessor set empty because it is the root?
Does the history of this entity form a linear chain or a directed acyclic graph with merge nodes?
When a revision has multiple predecessors, what merge strategy produced it and was any predecessor content discarded?
Is the predecessor set closed and verifiable, or may it be incomplete because of import, embargo or disposition?
Are cycles, self-references and dangling predecessor references structurally prohibited and actually validated?
Is this a revision of the same entity, a derivation into a new entity, or only a new format or rendition of unchanged content?
What test distinguishes 'substantial content retained, therefore a revision' from 'a new entity'?
Does a change of entity identifier accompany this change, and on what grounds?
Are the two records alternates of one another, or specialisations of a shared abstract entity?
Which external or upstream artefact versions were consumed to produce this revision?
Is each upstream reference pinned to an immutable version and digest, or does it point at a moving target?
How is an upstream version withdrawal, re-tagging or yank detected after this revision was produced?
What is recorded when upstream provenance is unavailable or cannot be verified?
Is this revision stored as a full state snapshot, as a forward delta against its predecessor, or as both?
Which patch or diff formalism expresses the delta, and at what version?
Are delta operations applied atomically, and what is the defined outcome when one operation fails?
Can the delta be verified to reproduce the successor state exactly, and against which digest?
Is the delta invertible so that the predecessor state can be recomputed from the successor?
What categories of change does this revision contain?
Is any change in this revision breaking for declared consumers of the declared public surface?
Does the change alter meaning, or only presentation, encoding or format?
Is this revision a correction of a previously published error, and does it supersede a published statement?
What concise human-readable statement describes what changed and why, and in which languages is it maintained?
Is the human-readable note guaranteed complete with respect to the machine-readable delta?
Is compatibility asserted for readers of newer data, for writers producing older data, or in both directions?
What evidence supports the compatibility claim, and can it be re-executed?
How are optional and defaulted elements treated when an older consumer reads data produced under this revision?
Is a migration required to adopt this revision, or is adoption transparent to existing instances and consumers?
What procedure moves an instance from the predecessor version to this revision, and in what order are its steps executed?
Is the migration reversible, and what is the documented rollback path?
Is the migration idempotent and safe to re-run after a partial failure?
What data loss, precision loss or semantic loss is expected and accepted by this migration?
Who is responsible for executing the migration, and by when must it complete?
Is this revision, or an element within it, deprecated, and from which instant does the deprecation take effect?
At which instant will the deprecated revision or endpoint stop being served, and is that instant at or after the deprecation instant?
What replacement is recommended, and where is the migration guidance published?
How is the deprecation signalled to consumers that only interact through the access interface?
At what instant did the change event occur, and at what separate instant was it recorded by the system of record?
Which clock and which offset are authoritative for the recorded instants, and is the timestamp computer-generated?
Is the recorded time monotonic across the revision sequence, and what is done when it is not?
What temporal precision is guaranteed, and is an independently attested timestamp required?
Over which period is the content of this revision asserted to be true in the world, as distinct from when it was recorded?
Does this revision correct the record for a past period, or does it apply only forward from its effective instant?
At which instant did the predecessor revision cease to be the record of truth?
When an as-of query is issued, is it resolved against record time or effective time, and how is the choice signalled?
What lifecycle states may a revision occupy, and which transitions between them are legal?
At which state does the revision become immutable, and what enforces immutability from that point?
Who may promote a working copy or draft to a released revision?
May a released revision return to draft, and if not, what is the substitute mechanism?
What happens to a working copy or checkout that is never checked in?
How is a withdrawal, retraction, deactivation or deletion represented in the history?
Does the withdrawal remove content, remove availability, or only mark status?
Is a tombstone published so that consumers can distinguish a deleted revision from one that never existed?
Can a withdrawn revision be reinstated, and under whose authority?
What reason is recorded for the withdrawal, and is that reason itself disclosable?
Which agent performed the change, and on whose behalf did they act?
Is the agent a person, an organisation or a software agent, and is that distinction recorded explicitly?
Is the identity of the agent verified, and by what means?
Which activity, process or job produced this revision?
Under what authority was this change permitted to be made?
Was formal approval required before release, who approved it, and at what instant?
What request, ticket or justification triggered the change?
What is the declared meaning of any signature applied to this revision?
Was an impact analysis performed before approval, and is its outcome retained?
What digest, computed over what canonical byte sequence, fixes the content of this revision?
Which canonicalisation rules are applied before digesting, and which fields are excluded from the digest scope?
How is a change of digest algorithm handled without invalidating historical fixity?
Who re-verifies fixity, how often, and what happens when verification fails?
Is any exposed access-interface validator distinct from the content digest, and is that distinction documented?
Is the change history append-only, and what technical and organisational controls enforce that?
Can a history entry be altered or removed, and does any such alteration itself leave a record that does not obscure the previous entry?
How is redaction of sensitive content in past revisions performed without destroying verifiability of the remaining history?
What cryptographically binds each history entry to its predecessor?
Who is technically capable of forging or suppressing a history entry, and which controls detect it?
How does a consumer enumerate the revisions of an entity, and is the enumeration complete, stably ordered and pageable?
How is the state of the entity as of a given instant retrieved?
How is a historical state reconstructed when only forward deltas are stored?
What are the cost and latency bounds of retrieving deep history, and is any part cold-stored?
How is a lost update prevented when two agents revise the same entity concurrently?
What precondition must an update carry, and what is returned when the precondition is not met?
How are conflicting concurrent revisions detected and resolved?
Is there an explicit lock or checkout model, and what happens to abandoned locks?
Is the change history visible to the same audience as the current state of the entity?
Which parts of a history entry may reveal personal data, security detail or confidential rationale?
Can a past revision be embargoed so that its existence is visible but its content is not?
Who may read agent identities, approval records and change reasons within the history?
How long must each revision and its history entry be retained, and on what basis?
May history be compacted, squashed or pruned, and what must survive compaction?
How is a lawful erasure or rectification request reconciled with an append-only, digest-chained history?
Who authorises disposition and what evidence of the disposition is retained afterwards?
Does a legal hold suspend disposition, and how is a held entry marked?
To which external vocabularies are the version fields of this model aligned, and at which version of each?
Is each mapping claimed as an alignment or as conformance, and what evidence supports a conformance claim?
Where do external models conflict with this model's semantics, and how is the conflict handled?
How are version relations exposed over an access interface that carries only links, headers or metadata properties?
Which alignments are lossy, and precisely what is lost in each direction?

grok_only.name: What version indicator string is assigned to this revision, and under which versioning scheme is it interpreted?
If Semantic Versioning is declared, what are the major, minor, patch, pre-release and build-metadata components and the computed precedence key?
Which master system or steward assigned the version indicator, and is that assignment unique within the series?
Is the recorded indicator a true version name rather than a date, checksum, or host identifier used as a substitute?
If a pre-release label is present, is the revision declared unstable and not required to meet the compatibility of the associated normal version?
What is the series, ontology, or canonical identifier of the unversioned resource this revision belongs to?
What version-specific IRI, DOI, or master-system identifier identifies this exact revision?
Should this revision be retrievable at the series identifier, only at the version identifier, or both because it is the current version?
Did this change mint a new persistent identifier, or reuse the previous identifier with an updated version label?
Is the combination of series identifier and version identifier unique, and are reserved-vocabulary IRIs avoided as version IRIs?
Is the host identifier a mutable permalink, an abstract series, or itself an immutable snapshot?
Which abstract or permalink resource does this snapshot specialise, and which other snapshots are its alternates?
Is the has-version link a DCAT/PAV lifecycle snapshot, or a broader DCMI edition or adaptation that should not be treated as a revision chain member?
Which snapshot is designated as the current equivalent content of the mutable resource?
What is the direct previous version of this revision, and is that link asserted as wasRevisionOf / previousVersion rather than a generic derivation?
Which earlier versions are known, either by walking the previousVersion chain or by explicit hasEarlierVersion links?
What next or successor version, if any, is recorded (adms:next, DataCite IsPreviousVersionOf inverse, or Dimension successor)?
Does this revision have more than one direct predecessor, as in a merge, even though PAV previousVersion is normally functional?
Has the operator confused dcat:prev (previous in a dataset series) with dcat:previousVersion (previous snapshot of the same resource)?
Which prior resource does this revision supplant, displace or supersede, and does the prior resource remain citable?
If persistent identifiers are used, is this identifier linked as IsNewVersionOf the previous edition and the previous as IsPreviousVersionOf this one?
Is only one version valid in this chain, as in successive drafts of a contract, or are historical snapshots still in force for citation?
Who authorised the replacement, and at what event time versus observation time?
What are all known versioned snapshots of this abstract or canonical resource?
Which snapshot is the current version, who designated it, and should the series IRI now resolve to it?
If a canonical identifier exists, is each specific version linked with HasVersion / IsVersionOf in both directions?
Are multiple snapshots simultaneously designated current (branches), which OWL series convention does not allow?
After a new current version is published, do prior versions remain resolvable at their version IRIs or DOIs?
Which prior versions is this revision declared incompatible with, and what consumer action is required before upgrade?
What change class is assigned (SemVer major/minor/patch, DataCite major/minor, or local), and who defined that class?
If the SemVer major component is zero, is the public API explicitly treated as unstable so that anything MAY change?
If this resource is imported with others, does the import closure mix versions of the same series or include an incompatibleWith pair?
Is the related resource a life-cycle revision, a broader edition or adaptation, a format variant, a series member, a translation, or a non-revision derivation?
Did the content change substantively, or only the format, encoding, or distribution?
If PROV derivation holds, is wasRevisionOf applicable, or should wasQuotedFrom, hadPrimarySource, or generic wasDerivedFrom be used instead?
What is the workflow status of this revision, from which concept scheme, and in which process?
Is this revision or any public contract it exposes marked deprecated, and did that trigger a minor version increment under SemVer?
Who is authorised to change status, and what evidence supports the current value?
Is a withdrawn or deprecated revision still backward compatible for consumers who already depend on it?
Has this revision been released, and is in-place mutation therefore forbidden?
At what event time was this revision generated, and at what time was that fact observed or ingested?
Has this revision been invalidated or withdrawn, at what time, and by which activity?
If dcterms:modified is set on a released revision, was that a forbidden in-place change or a metadata-only update that DataCite would treat as a minor version on the same identifier?
Are issued and modified times those of the resource revision, not the catalog record listing times?
What is the description of changes between this version and the previous version, in which language?
If there are backward compatibility issues with the previous version, are they described in the version notes?
Who authored or approved the version notes, and is that distinct from the content author recorded in Provenance?
Do the notes cover added, removed, deprecated and incompatible contracts, or only a marketing summary?
From which source revision to which target revision does this migration patch apply?
What ordered operations constitute the patch, and did a test operation fail?
Must consumers apply a migration (data rewrite, mapping, or recompile) before using this revision, given declared incompatibilities?
If the host is not JSON-shaped, what equivalent sequential delta form is used, and is JSON Patch only an alignment?
Who may apply the patch, and is application blocked when the target is a frozen released version?
What checksum algorithm and digest identify the frozen bits of this revision or its distribution?
What concurrency token or If-Match value must be supplied before a patch or status change is accepted?
Has any comparison shown that a released revision's content changed after freeze?
How long must prior versions remain resolvable at their version identifiers, and when may a version be deleted or only tombstoned?
Do retained prior versions contain personal data that requires a different retention or redaction exception than the current version?

requirements: Resolve every provider-only bundle, layer and finding against primary evidence.
Resolve the model boundary and entry kind before accepting structure.
Verify live URLs and version pins for all accepted sources.
Record every rejected and deferred node with a reason.
Do not publish while any critical conflict remains unresolved.
